text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock has drifted up 0.31% today, capping a strong two-week gain of 7.81%. The move reflects a broader rally driven by Middle East tensions — escalating strikes between the U.S. and Iran have pushed crude oil prices to six-week highs, with Brent nearing $100 per barrel. For a refiner like Marathon, higher crude prices often support margins when refineries are running near capacity, which they are at 98%, and the company can pass costs through to gasoline and diesel sales already hitting record prices at the pump.

The refiner's sustained momentum over the past week aligns with tightening oil markets and strong refinery utilization. With crude inventories at 711 million barrels and gasoline storage relatively tight at 206 million barrels, the supply-demand dynamic favors active refiners converting expensive crude into finished products consumers need to buy regardless of price.
